$comment: Single source of truth for the set of dakota image variants and which
pipeline roles each variant participates in. See issue #1434.
Adding or removing a variant is a single edit here. Every variant MUST
declare a membership decision for EVERY role in `roles` below: either a
participation object, or {"excluded": "<reason>"}. There is no implicit
membership, so a forgotten variant fails the check-publish-workflow gate
closed instead of silently reducing pipeline coverage.
Roles with "derived": true are the ones publish.yml's matrices must match.
.github/scripts/image_variants.py projects this file into each role's
matrix and the check-publish-workflow gate fails if publish.yml has drifted
from it, so the restated copies can no longer diverge unnoticed. Replacing
those inline matrices with `fromJSON` of this file is the follow-up phase;
it needs a token with the `workflows` permission, which the agent App does
not hold. Run `image_variants.py --role <role>` to get the exact payload.
Roles with "derived": false are still restated literally in their own
workflow, in a grammar with no matrix to compare (a JSON literal, a shell
`for` list, per-variant named steps). Those are gated on image names:
`check_consumer_membership` fails the gate if a consumer stops naming an
image declared for its role, or starts naming one this file excludes.
Reconciling their *membership* — whether the gaming variants should be
smoke-tested, scanned and rolled back at all — remains a maintainer
behavior decision tracked by #1434, NOT a mechanical refactor.

sbom.excluded: no SBOM entry wired for gaming builds yet

smoke.excluded: publish-smoke.yml has never covered the gaming variants (#1434)

scan.excluded: vulnerability-scan.yml has never covered the gaming variants (#1434)
